questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
questions.question: A non uniform beam of weight 120 N pivoted at one end is shown in the diagram below. Calculate the value of F to keep the beam in equilibrium.
questions.solution: Weight of beam produces a clockwise moment and applied force F produces an anticlockwise moment (balancing). Equating moments: 120 x 0.2 = F x 0.8, so F = 30 N.

marking_points.point: Principle of moments: clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment
Substitution 120 x 0.2 = F x 0.8 and F = 30 N

questions.figure_desc: Beam pivoted at one end; weight 120 N acts at 0.2 m from the pivot (centre of gravity) and force F acts at 0.8 m from the pivot.

questions.question:
Meera chose to use a block and tackle system of '9' pulleys instead of a single movable pulley to lift a heavy load.
(a) What is the advantage of using a block and tackle system over a single movable pulley?
(b) Why should she connect more number of pulleys in the upper fixed block?
questions.solution:
(a) Mechanical advantage of a block and tackle of 9 pulleys is 9, whereas that of a single movable pulley is 2.
(b) Increasing the number of pulleys increases the mechanical advantage.

marking_points.point: More pulleys give higher mechanical advantage / VR

questions.question: A fuse is rated 5 A. Can it be used with a geyser rated 1540 W, 220 V. Write Yes or No. Give supporting calculations to justify your answer.

concepts: TIR and colour dependence of critical angle
questions.question:
(a) Why do we use red colour as a danger signal on the top of a skyscraper?
(b) The diagram below shows the path of a blue ray through the prism:
1. Calculate the critical angle of the material of the prism for blue colour.
2. What is the measure of the angle of this prism (A)?
3. Which colour should replace the blue ray, for the ray to undergo Total Internal Reflection?
questions.solution:
(a) Red is scattered least due to its longest wavelength in the visible range, so it is visible from a very long distance.
(b) 1. Critical angle = 43 degrees (ray meets the second face at 43 deg, emerging along the surface at 90 deg... per figure 47 + 43 = 90).
2. Angle of prism = 43 degrees.
3. Indigo or violet; their critical angles are less than that of blue, so the 43 deg angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle and TIR occurs.

marking_points.point: Red scattered least / longest wavelength, visible from far
Indigo or violet with reason (smaller critical angle)

questions.figure_desc: Prism ABC with a blue ray entering one face and meeting the other face; angles marked 47 deg, 43 deg, 133 deg and 90 deg; angle of incidence on the second face is 43 deg (equal to the critical angle).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Refractive index from speed of light
questions.question:
Light travels a distance of '10x' units in time 't1' in vacuum and it travels a distance of 'x' units in time 't2' in a denser medium. Using this information answer the question that follows:
(a) 'Light covers a distance of '20x' units in time 't1' in diamond.' State true or false.
(b) Calculate the refractive index of the medium in terms of 't1' and 't2'.
questions.solution:
(a) False. Diamond is denser than vacuum, so light cannot cover a longer distance than in vacuum in the same time.
(b) Speed in vacuum = 10x/t1; speed in medium = x/t2; refractive index = (10x/t1)/(x/t2) = 10 t2 / t1.

marking_points.point: Speeds in vacuum and medium written

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: conservation of mechanical energy with friction
questions.question:
Two identical marbles A and B are rolled down along Path 1 and Path 2 respectively. Path 1 is frictionless and Path 2 is rough.
(a) Which marble will surely reach the next peak?
(b) Along which path/s the mechanical energy will be conserved?
(c) Along which path/s is the law of conservation of energy obeyed?
questions.solution:
(a) Marble A (Path 1 is frictionless).
(b) Mechanical energy is conserved along Path 1 only, where there is no friction. (The printed board key says both paths; either is accepted.)
(c) The law of conservation of energy is obeyed along both paths, since energy lost to friction on Path 2 appears as heat.

marking_points.point: Mechanical energy conserved: Path 1 (frictionless); printed key says both, accept either
Law of conservation of energy: both paths (friction converts energy to heat)

questions.figure_desc: Two tracks with a hill/valley profile; marble A on Path 1 (frictionless) and marble B on Path 2 (rough), each to reach the next peak.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: frequency vs length of air column
questions.question:
In the given diagram, a vibrating tuning fork is kept near the mouth of a burette filled with water. The length of the air column is adjusted by opening the tap of the burette. At a length of 5 cm of the air column, a loud sound is heard.
(a) Name the phenomenon illustrated by the above experiment.
(b) Why is a loud sound heard at this particular length?
(c) If the present tuning fork is replaced with a tuning fork of higher frequency, should the length of the air column increase or decrease to produce a loud sound? Give a reason.
questions.solution:
(a) Resonance
(b) The natural frequency of the air column matched with the frequency of the tuning fork.
(c) The length of the air column should decrease, since frequency is inversely proportional to the length of the air column.

marking_points.point: Natural frequency of air column equals tuning fork frequency
Reason: frequency inversely proportional to length

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: ohmic vs non-ohmic from V-I data
questions.question:
The voltage - current readings of a certain material are shown in the table given below:
Voltage (V): 10 V, 20 V, 30 V
Current (I): 2 A, 3 A, 4 A
Study the table.
(a) State whether the conductor used is ohmic or non-ohmic.
(b) Justify your answer.
(c) State Ohm's law.
questions.solution:
(a) Non-ohmic
(b) The resistance (V/I = 5, 6.67, 7.5 ohm) is not constant; it increases as voltage and current increase.
(c) The current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it, provided physical conditions (temperature etc.) remain constant.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Study the diagram: a circuit with a 4 V cell; one arm has 10 ohm and 6 ohm resistors in series, the other arm has 12 ohm and 4 ohm resistors in series, the two arms being in parallel across the cell.
(a) Calculate the total resistance of the circuit.
(b) Calculate the current drawn from the cell.
(c) State whether the current through 10 ohm resistor is greater than, less than or equal to the current through the 12 ohm resistor.
questions.solution:
(a) 10 + 6 = 16 ohm; 12 + 4 = 16 ohm; the two arms are in parallel, so R = 8 ohm.
(b) I = V/R = 4/8 = 0.5 A.
(c) Equal, since both arms have the same resistance.
questions.figure_desc: Circuit: 4 V cell connected across two parallel arms, arm 1 = 10 ohm and 6 ohm in series, arm 2 = 12 ohm and 4 ohm in series.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
concepts: calorimetry principle of mixtures with ice
questions.question:
85 g of water at 30°C is cooled to 5°C by adding certain mass of ice. Find the mass of ice required.
[Specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 Jg-1 C-1, Specific latent heat of fusion = 336 Jg-1]
questions.solution: Heat lost by water = 85 x 4.2 x (30 - 5) = 8925 J. Heat gained by ice = m x 336 + m x 4.2 x (5 - 0) = 357 m. Equating: m = 8925/357 = 25 g.

marking_points.point: Heat lost by water 85 x 4.2 x 25
Heat gained by ice m x 336 + m x 4.2 x 5, equated

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
(a) Why does it become pleasantly warm when the lakes start freezing?
(b) Water freezes to form ice. What change would you expect in the average kinetic energy of the molecules?
(c) Which will contain more heat energy 1 g of ice at 0°C or 1 g water at 0°C?
questions.solution:
(a) When a lake freezes it releases latent heat to the atmosphere, which warms the surroundings.
(b) No change, since the temperature does not change (stays 0 deg C).
(c) 1 g of water at 0 deg C contains more heat energy than 1 g of ice at 0 deg C, because water has absorbed the latent heat of fusion. (The printed board key states ice, which is physically incorrect; either answer is accepted.)

marking_points.point: Latent heat released to surroundings on freezing
No change in average kinetic energy (temperature constant)
Water at 0 deg C has more heat energy than ice (printed key says ice; accept either)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: AC generator; magnetic effect of current
concepts: oersted compass deflection and field strength
questions.question:
(a) State one factor that affects the magnitude of induced current in an AC generator.
(b) Given below is a circuit to study the magnetic effect of electric current. ABCD is a cardboard kept perpendicular to the conductor XY. A magnetic compass is placed at the point P of the cardboard. P1 and P2 are the positions of the magnetic compass, before and after passing a current through XY respectively.
1. Name the rule that is used to predict the direction of deflection of the magnetic compass.
2. State the direction of current in the conductor (X to Y or Y to X) when the circuit is complete.
3. If resistance R is increased, then what will be the effect on the magnetic lines of force around the conductor?
questions.solution:
(a) Number of turns in the armature may be increased.
(b) 1. Maxwell's right hand thumb rule.
2. Deflection being clockwise, the current is from X to Y.
3. As R increases, current decreases, so the magnetic field weakens and the density of magnetic lines of force decreases.

marking_points.point: One factor e.g. number of turns / speed / field strength
Density of field lines decreases (field weaker)

questions.figure_desc: Vertical conductor XY through a cardboard ABCD carrying a compass at P (positions P1 before, P2 after current); a DC supply and resistor R in series; needle shown deflected clockwise.
